svg.text: BLOOM FILTER — THE BIT ARRAY, STEP BY STEP
THE STRUCTURE — one BitSet, m bits, all zero. That is the whole filter.
TOY SIZING for this walk-through: m = 16 bits, k = 3 probes
Real code: BloomFilterConfig(n=1000, p=0.01) ⇒ m = 9,586 bits (1.2 KB), k = 7.
Same mechanics, just wider. NO keys are stored anywhere — only bits.
add("apple") — hash k times with seed = i, set every bit it lands on
one loop, k iterations ⇒ add() is O(k) — n never appears ✓
the seed IS the probe index — k positions from ONE strategy
add("mango") — bit 9 was ALREADY 1. Setting it again is a no-op, and it is now shared.
bit 9 already set by "apple" ⇒ no counter, no owner recorded
THIS is why remove() cannot exist: clearing bit 9 to
fix = Counting Bloom Filter: 4-bit counters instead of bits
mightContain(x) — probe the SAME k positions. Exactly three things can happen.
All k bits are 1, so we return true.
One clear bit is proof: had "grape"
Early exit ⇒ negatives are the fast path.
No single key set all three — two
This is the tax you pay for O(m) bits.
THE FALSE-POSITIVE RATE — memorise these three
probability all k bits are already 1
bits needed for a target p
probes that leave the array ~half full
This repo reports the EMPIRICAL version instead: estimatedFalsePositiveRate() = (bits.cardinality() / m)^k — measured fill, not predicted.
add / mightContain: O(k) — constant, independent of how many keys are in
space: m bits total. 1M keys at p=1% ≈ 1.2 MB — a HashSet would be ~50 MB
thread-safety here: synchronized on add AND mightContain (one lock, no parallel reads)
classic use: skip the disk/network lookup for keys that are definitely absent (LSM SSTables, CDN caches, crawler URL dedupe)
